title: 3D viewer for Arches — architecture
summary: The parts implied by the planning session, and how they connect. Nothing here is built yet: this is the shape the conversation arrived at, with the boundaries that were argued for and the questions that would change them.

source.title: 3D viewer widget integration for multiple file formats

parts.label: Digital Object
parts.purpose: The Arches resource that holds a 3D file, its format, its derivatives and a processing status, and links to the Monument or site it depicts.
parts.why_split: Everything else binds to this. The widget needs to know which node holds the file; the search filter needs whatever metadata is worth filtering on. It is the contract the rest of the design rests on.
responsibilities: Point at the original uploaded file
List derivative files produced at ingest
Link to the resource the model depicts
not: Storing file bytes — that is the file store
open: Is this the standard Arches reference data model or customised?
Is there already a node for the file, and one for format?
Does a Monument link to it via a resource-instance node, so a viewer can be reused without duplicating storage?
What model metadata is worth capturing at ingest — poly count, textures, scan date?

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: What does your current Digital Object graph look like

parts.label: Upload handling
parts.purpose: Accepts a 3D file against a Digital Object, stores the original untouched, and enqueues a conversion job.
parts.why_split: The decision that conversion happens at ingest rather than at view time puts a queue boundary right here. Upload has to return before conversion finishes.
not: Deciding which renderer will be used

parts.label: Conversion worker
parts.purpose: A background worker that picks up conversion jobs, runs the right converter for the format, writes derivatives back and flips the status.
parts.why_split: nxsbuild on a 50-million-triangle mesh takes minutes to hours. Nothing in a request cycle can wait for that.
responsibilities: Select converter by format and size
not: Deciding the tier at view time — the widget does that from what exists
open: Same-server Celery worker to start, or a dedicated conversion pod? Start simple, split if load appears.
Which node pool on AKS if CPU pressure shows up?

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: I'd start with the same-server Celery approach

parts.label: PotreeConverter 2.x
parts.purpose: Converts LAS/LAZ/PLY/PTX point clouds into a static octree directory that can be served as flat files.
parts.why_split: Third-party C++ binary. It is a dependency of the worker, not something we write or control.

parts.label: Nexus converter
parts.purpose: Builds the multiresolution NXZ representation used for meshes too large to load whole.
parts.why_split: Only runs for the heavy tier, and brings a packaging problem the other converters do not.
open: Ships officially as Windows binaries — how does it run in a Kubernetes ingest pipeline?
Accepts only PLY and OBJ, so anything else needs a conversion before the conversion

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: Nexus has a Three.js loader built in

parts.label: DWG converter
parts.purpose: Would turn AutoCAD DWG into something a browser can read — DWF, IFC or GLTF.
parts.why_split: DWG has no browser path at all, so it needs a step nothing else needs, with a licensing question attached.
open: ODA File Converter is free only for non-commercial use — the Queensland work is commercial
Autodesk APS is the alternative; cost and data-residency unexamined

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: DWG still needs its own conversion step regardless

parts.label: File store
parts.purpose: Holds originals and derivative files, and serves them to the browser.
parts.why_split: Streaming renderers need HTTP range requests. Whether the store supports them decides whether the heavy tier works at all.
responsibilities: Serve octree chunks and NXZ files
open: S3-compatible blob storage, or local filesystem behind Django?
If Django is serving these, does range-request support come for free or need work?

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: what's your storage backend for these files?

parts.label: Viewer widget
parts.purpose: One Arches widget bound to a Digital Object's file node. Looks at which derivatives exist and hands off to the right renderer.
parts.why_split: Keeping the Arches integration in one component means the tile binding, permissions and card template are written once, even though the renderers underneath do genuinely different work.
responsibilities: Choose a renderer from available derivatives
open: Knockout for v7 or Vue on the v8 trajectory?

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: one widget component, but with two rendering modes

parts.label: Online 3D Viewer
parts.purpose: Tier-1 renderer. Loads the original file directly for the wide format spread, up to roughly 50MB.
parts.why_split: Vendored third-party library with its own Three.js and its own UI. We call it; we do not maintain it.
not: Anything streamed or multiresolution — it loads whole files

parts.label: Nexus renderer
parts.purpose: Tier-2 mesh renderer. NexusObject in a Three.js scene, streaming an NXZ derivative.
parts.why_split: Separated from 3DHOP deliberately — the streaming is usable without adopting that framework's viewer or its licence.

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: the multiresolution streaming tech and 3DHOP's viewer UI are actually separable

parts.label: Potree renderer
parts.purpose: Point cloud renderer. Streams octree chunks so only what is in view at the current zoom is loaded.
parts.why_split: Points are not triangles — its camera controls, measurement and clipping semantics are its own, so it stays a distinct renderer even inside the shared widget.

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: the standard for web point cloud viewing

parts.label: Search filter
parts.purpose: An Arches search filter that narrows results to resources with 3D data, with format facets and thumbnails.
parts.why_split: Extending search keeps permissions, saved searches, export and spatial filters for free. A separate browse page loses all four.
open: What does "filter by model" actually mean — format, subject, or model properties?

parts.label: 3D browser plugin
parts.purpose: A dedicated page for browsing and comparing 3D models, with its own routing and state.
parts.why_split: Deferred, not dropped. Only justified if search genuinely cannot do the job — side-by-side comparison, a spatial 3D browser, or a curated gallery distinct from search.

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: A plugin is a bigger commitment

edges.label: original
edges.note: The original is always preserved, whatever derivatives get made later.

edges.label: enqueue
edges.note: The asynchronous boundary. Upload returns immediately; conversion finishes later.

edges.label: register derivatives
edges.note: This write is what the widget later reads to pick a renderer, so the derivative list is the real interface between conversion and viewing.

edges.label: range requests
edges.note: This is the edge that makes the storage question load-bearing rather than incidental.

edges.label: opens
edges.note: Search results lead back into the resource report where the widget lives.
